after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Given that $⟨\,\cdot \,,\,\cdot \,⟩$ is the standard Hermitian inner product over $C,$ find $⟨a,\,b-(1+3\text{i})c⟩$ if 

$\,$ $⟨b,a⟩=1+\text{i}\,$ and $\,⟨a,c⟩=2.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that the inner product over $C$ satisfies the following properties. 

- It is linear in the first argument. For any $a,b,c\in {C}^{n}$ and any $\alpha \in C,$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a+b,c⟩=⟨a,c⟩+⟨b,c⟩\,$ and $\,⟨\alpha a,b⟩=\alpha ⟨a,b⟩.$

- It is antilinear in the second argument. For any $a,b,c\in {C}^{n}$ and any $\alpha \in C,$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,b+c⟩=⟨a,b⟩+⟨a,c⟩\,$ and $\,⟨a,\alpha b⟩=\overset{―}{\alpha }⟨a,b⟩.$

- It has conjugate symmetry. For any $a,b\in {C}^{n},$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,b⟩=\overset{―}{⟨b,a⟩}.$

- It is positive-definite. For any $a\in {C}^{n},$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,a⟩$ is a non-negative real number, and $⟨a,a⟩=0$ if and only if $a=0.$

First, we use the fact that the inner product over $C$ is antilinear in the second argument:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨a,\,b-(1+3\text{i})c⟩ & =⟨a,b⟩-⟨a,(1+3\text{i})c⟩ \\  & =⟨a,b⟩-(\overset{―}{1+3\text{i}})⟨a,c⟩ \\  & =⟨a,b⟩-(1-3\text{i})⟨a,c⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that the inner product over $C$ has conjugate symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨a,b⟩-(1-3\text{i})⟨a,c⟩ & =\overset{―}{⟨b,a⟩}-(1-3\text{i})⟨a,c⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute the values for $⟨b,a⟩$ and $⟨a,c⟩:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{⟨b,a⟩}-(1-3\text{i})⟨a,c⟩ & =\overset{―}{1+\text{i}}-(1-3\text{i})\cdot 2 \\  & =1-\text{i}-2+6\text{i} \\  & =-1+5\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$
